web_delivery: Next.js/Vite PWA on Vercel hobby, Supabase Postgres full-text search for the index; no uploads or media hosting (thumbnails hot-linked or omitted).
satellite_what: Free page converting yarn weight names (US/UK/AU), hook and needle sizes and gauge swatches to stitch counts.
marketing_where: Pinterest pattern boards; Ravelry forums and Facebook crochet groups (read the rules first); craft blog directories and designer newsletters; Product Hunt
marketing_target: Budget crocheters and knitters who are tired of Pro-only pattern apps.
marketing_funnel: Free converter or collection page -> index search -> email list of new free patterns.
cold_outreach: Offer small designers a free listing that drives traffic back to their own site with their ads intact.
post_ideas: I built a free pattern search that never hides patterns behind a paywall | Why pattern apps keep going Pro-only and what designers lose | Every free amigurumi pattern under 2 hours, filtered by yarn weight
competitors: AllFreeCrochet advanced search; Yarnspirations / Lion Brand / LoveCrafts free collections; YarnPal
notes: Weakest point: individual sites already have filters, and dataset building is manual. Strong, recent, high-volume review signal though. Designer consent/robots rules must be respected; index only titles and links.

name: AAC Board Hub
idea: Free web AAC board editor with backup, sharing and ready-made therapist-built page sets so a family never loses years of setup.
description: Parents and speech therapists build symbol-and-word boards for non-speaking children or adults, speak them with the browser's built-in speech, and keep them backed up in the cloud so a broken tablet does not wipe years of customisation. Boards can be shared as links or copied from a library of page sets that follow common core-word layouts. Hard to copy because the value is the board import/export plumbing and vetted vocabulary page sets, not the grid UI.
why_hard_to_copy: Importing and exporting boards between AAC systems and curating vetted core-vocabulary page sets takes speech-language-pathology knowledge; the UI alone is a weekend project.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel using the Web Speech API for voice and IndexedDB for offline boards; board JSON and shared links in Supabase; symbols limited to openly licensed sets.
marketing_where: speech-language pathologist and special-education teacher groups; AAC parent Facebook groups; disability-focused conferences and newsletters; Product Hunt
marketing_target: Families and SLPs who cannot afford or cannot restore expensive AAC apps
marketing_funnel: Free boards and backup for individuals, then paid for clinics managing many clients
cold_outreach: Offer SLP bloggers free page sets built to their preferred core-word framework.
post_ideas: How to back up your child's AAC setup before the tablet breaks | A free core-word starter board you can copy and edit | What AAC apps cost in 2026 and what you can do for free
competitors: Cboard; Vocable AAC; Proloquo2Go; TouchChat
notes: Cboard is already a free open-source web AAC app, so this is only worth doing as a better-curated, backed-up alternative or as contributions to Cboard; the strength of the signal is cost and lost-setup stories, not a missing web product. High-stakes users: needs reliability and an SLP advisor. Symbol licensing (e.g., commercial symbol sets) must be avoided.

name: TicketAccess
idea: A guide to which local transit and bus tickets foreigners can actually buy without a local phone number or domestic card.
description: Per operator pages say whether online purchase needs a local phone number or card, which apps accept foreign cards or PayPal, whether ticket machines or on-board cash work, and the workaround that visitors report works. The moat is a curated, tested directory of operators across countries; generic maps and trip planners never document payment friction.
why_hard_to_copy: Hands-on curated directory of payment and verification friction by operator, kept current by traveller reports; not available from any API.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; operators table in Supabase with last_tested date; submission form for traveller reports.
marketing_where: FlyerTalk forums; TripAdvisor destination forums; Travel Stack Exchange (answer questions, link only where site rules allow); Facebook expat and digital-nomad groups; Show HN; Product Hunt
marketing_target: Visitors to countries with phone-number-gated ticketing (India, US commuter rail, Spain buses)
marketing_funnel: Search 'buy <transit> ticket without local phone number'.
cold_outreach: Ask transport enthusiasts and expat forum moderators for tested workarounds.
post_ideas: Buying NJ Transit tickets as a tourist without a US SIM | Bengaluru metro tickets for foreigners: what works | Spanish bus tickets with a foreign card
notes: Searched for a competitor and found none for this specific problem. Only three signals and the dataset is wide and shallow; value depends on community contributions. Included as an honest low-confidence idea.

name: BackSide
idea: In-browser tool that pairs the front and back scans of old prints into one record with a caption, written as standard XMP/EXIF metadata.
description: Drop flatbed scans or phone shots; the tool pairs front and back by filename or order, auto-crops and straightens each print, keeps the handwritten back as a linked second image or panel, and lets you type who, where and when once. The caption and approximate date are embedded as standard XMP/IPTC fields so they survive in Google Photos or genealogy software, and everything exports as a ZIP without uploading anything. Aimed at families digitizing albums. Hard to copy only moderately: the moat is a polished client-side crop/deskew/pairing workflow and correct metadata writing, which store-bought phone apps do not combine.
why_hard_to_copy: Client-side image pipeline (edge detection, perspective and page-curve correction) plus correct XMP/IPTC/EXIF writing with partial dates, wrapped in a pairing workflow; a weekend clone would skip the curved-page and metadata correctness.
web_delivery: PWA: getUserMedia for phone capture or file drop for flatbed scans, OpenCV.js/WASM or canvas code for crop and deskew, File System Access API / ZIP download for output; no server.
satellite_what: Enter the print size and the goal (screen, 4x6 reprint, 8x10) and get the recommended scan DPI, pixel dimensions and TIFF/JPEG file size.
marketing_where: WikiTree G2G forum; RootsChat genealogy forum; Genealogy Stack Exchange; Local genealogy and historical society newsletters
marketing_target: Family historians and relatives digitizing shoeboxes of prints
marketing_funnel: DPI calculator or forum answer -> BackSide demo with sample scans -> batch of a whole album -> ZIP shared with relatives
cold_outreach: Offer genealogical society volunteers a free 'scanning day' workflow sheet that uses the tool.
post_ideas: Scan front and back of every photo and keep the caption: a no-upload workflow | What DPI should you scan old prints at? | Embedding names and dates in scans so they survive Google Photos
competitors: Photomyne; Google PhotoScan
notes: Three independent SE requests, but each has very low engagement (28-65 views). The category is served by Photomyne (paid) and PhotoScan, so differentiation is front+back pairing, standard metadata and no-upload/no-subscription. Be honest that a basic version is a weekend project; the quality of crop/deskew is the real work.

name: Pitch Plan
idea: Tournament-day and mini-league planner for youth clubs: fixtures across pitches and time slots, live standings with sport-specific tiebreakers, and a printable end-of-season report.
description: Parents and volunteer coaches running youth tournaments and small leagues ask their team-manager app for tournament mode, league tables, league-calendar import and a printable season report, and the vendor has kept those on 'planned' for a year or more. Pitch Plan generates round-robin and pool-plus-knockout schedules for several divisions sharing limited pitches, with rest-time and duplicate-opponent constraints, then publishes a public standings page and a one-page PDF season report. All solver and tiebreaker logic runs in the browser so it fits the free tiers.
capital_note: Domain only; all compute is client-side.
why_hard_to_copy: Constraint-based fixture scheduling (shared pitches, rest gaps, balanced home/away, multi-division) and per-sport tiebreaker rules are correctness-critical and fiddly; plain bracket makers are easy, a trustworthy multi-field scheduler is not.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel Hobby; scheduling solver in a Web Worker client-side; Supabase free stores tournaments and results; public read-only standings URL; print CSS for PDF report.
satellite_what: Enter teams, pitches, start time, match length; get a printable schedule instantly.
marketing_where: Youth football/soccer club Facebook groups; Local league secretary forums; Coach forums and Discord servers; SportsPress/WordPress club-site communities; Product Hunt
marketing_target: Volunteer tournament organisers and league secretaries of youth clubs (soccer, hockey, handball)
marketing_funnel: Free fixture generator -> share link to standings -> organiser creates a free account to save and publish
cold_outreach: Offer to generate a club's next tournament schedule for free and ask for feedback.
post_ideas: How to schedule 12 teams on 3 pitches without anyone playing back-to-back | Free U10 tournament schedule generator with printable sheets | What tiebreakers youth leagues actually use and how to automate them
competitors: LeagueLobster scheduler; Tournify; Mingle Sport
notes: Signals come from one vendor board (Mingle Sport), several older than 12 months, but the vendor activity on them in 2026 and merged duplicates show the demand persists. Competitors exist (LeagueLobster free generator, Tournify), so the pitch must be the multi-pitch constraint quality plus the free printable season report. Mingle has no public API, so this is standalone, not an add-on.

name: Ruby Reader
idea: Add furigana to a Japanese EPUB or text in the browser, hide the readings you already know, and export a Kindle-friendly file.
description: Drop a Japanese EPUB; a client-side tokenizer and dictionary add ruby readings, you set your JLPT level or paste a known-word list so only unknown kanji get furigana, and it exports an EPUB with ruby that renders on e-readers or a fallback layout where ruby is not supported. Aimed at Japanese learners reading real books on Kindle or Kobo.
why_hard_to_copy: Correct reading selection in context (names, counters, rendaku), per-device ruby quirks on Kindle/Kobo and EPUB repackaging fidelity are fiddly; but open-source CLIs already do the base conversion.
web_delivery: Static web app on Vercel; kuromoji-style tokenizer and dictionary loaded client-side; EPUB unzipped, modified and re-zipped in the browser; nothing uploaded.
satellite_what: Free page: paste Japanese text, get ruby readings with a JLPT-level filter.
marketing_where: Japanese-learning Discords and forums; Hacker News Show HN; Lemmy language-learning communities; MobileRead forums (e-reader users); Anki forum Japanese threads
marketing_target: Japanese learners reading native ebooks on Kindle, Kobo or tablets.
marketing_funnel: Free paste tool -> free EPUB conversion for short books -> unlock for long novels.
cold_outreach: Answer 'how do I get furigana on my Kindle' questions.
post_ideas: Furigana only for the kanji you do not know yet | Why furigana breaks on Kindle and how to fix an EPUB | Convert a Japanese novel to learner mode in your browser
competitors: furigana4epub; Furiganalyse; Shiritai (Firefox add-on); Obsidian Furigana Generator
notes: Demand evidence is one thread of comments. Existing CLI tools do the heavy part; the opening is no-install, JLPT filtering and device testing. Dictionary data licenses (JMdict/UniDic) must be respected.

name: Seat Solver
idea: Paste a messy guest list and get it cleaned, grouped into households and seated automatically with keep-together and keep-apart rules.
description: People planning a wedding or party hand-assemble guest lists from texts, photos of address books and spreadsheets, then try to seat guests by trial and error. Seat Solver imports pasted lists and CSVs, merges duplicates, groups households, takes simple rules (sit with, keep apart, table sizes) and solves a seating plan you can drag to adjust and print. The moat is the optimisation (an NP-complete seating problem needing a good heuristic) plus robust list cleaning.
why_hard_to_copy: Seating is an NP-complete constraint problem; a solid heuristic (simulated annealing with weighted preferences) plus tolerant guest-list parsing is more than a drag-and-drop canvas.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; solver runs client-side in a Web Worker; Supabase only for saved plans; print-to-PDF layout.
satellite_what: Paste or upload a messy guest list; it merges duplicates, splits couples/households and exports a tidy CSV.
marketing_where: Wedding planning forums and Facebook groups; Pinterest-style wedding boards; Product Hunt; Hacker News Show HN
marketing_target: Couples and party hosts with 50-200 guests.
marketing_funnel: Free guest-list cleaner -> seating solver -> printable chart.
cold_outreach: Offer free solves to day-of coordinators who run several events a year.
post_ideas: Seating a wedding is a constraint problem: here is the maths | Merging four guest lists without duplicates | Keep-apart rules that never create an unseatable table
competitors: Tablecharm; SeatLogic; Seatplan.io
notes: Paid competitors at $29-40 one-time exist, so free needs a clear solver advantage. Demand evidence is anecdotal.

name: Recipe Box Anywhere
idea: A free-to-start web recipe box that works on every device and household member for one account, with one-click import of Paprika, Crouton and Recipe Keeper exports.
description: Recipe-manager buyers keep getting burned by per-device purchases (pay again for Android, Windows, a spouse's phone) and by paywalls that cap or lock saved recipes. This is a browser/PWA recipe box with household sharing and read-only share links for non-users, plus drag-and-drop importers that read the proprietary export files of the big native apps entirely client-side. The moat is the file-format importers (Paprika archive, Crouton, Recipe Keeper, plain text/Google Doc paste) and a robust ingredient/step parser, not the CRUD.
capital_note: Domain only; Supabase and Vercel free tiers
why_hard_to_copy: Correct importers for several proprietary export formats plus a tolerant ingredient and step parser (fractions, units, section headings, messy blog markup) take real iteration; a weekend CRUD clone would not read Paprika/Crouton archives or survive messy sources.
web_delivery: Next.js PWA on Vercel hobby; Supabase auth + Postgres with row-level security for household sharing; importers and recipe-scraping parser run in the browser or in a small serverless function reading schema.org Recipe JSON-LD.
satellite_what: Drop a Paprika, Crouton or Recipe Keeper export and get clean Markdown, JSON or printable PDF locally in the browser.
marketing_where: Hacker News Show HN; Product Hunt; Lemmy c/selfhosted and c/cooking; Mac Power Users and other app-switcher forums; cooking Facebook groups for Paprika users
marketing_target: Home cooks who bought Paprika, Recipe Keeper or Crouton and now use a mix of iPhone, Android and Windows, plus couples sharing one recipe collection
marketing_funnel: Free converter page -> import into the box -> share link to spouse -> household invite
cold_outreach: Reply in forum threads asking for a cross-platform recipe app with the converter link as the answer
post_ideas: I got tired of paying for the same recipe app four times, so I built a free one | Export your Paprika recipes to Markdown in your browser, nothing uploaded | Why your recipe app should not lock your recipes behind a subscription
competitors: Mealie; Tandoor Recipes; Paprika; Recipe Keeper
notes: Crowded space; moat rests on importers and parser quality and on free hosted sharing. Social-video caption import (Instagram/TikTok) is another recurring gap on Paprika (about 8 reviews, e.g. 2026-10-13, 2026-01-12) but Meta blocks scraping and newer apps (ReciMe, Recipy, Qwikdish) already cover it, so it is a stretch goal, not the core.

name: Lesson Reflow
idea: A teacher pacing calendar where lessons flow forward day by day but chosen lessons stay locked to a date, with holidays, in-service days and A/B or weekend schedules handled.
description: Teachers and homeschoolers on Common Curriculum have asked for a decade to pin a test, assembly or live lesson to a date while the other lesson cards bump forward around it. Lesson Reflow is a drag-and-drop pacing calendar: the user defines the school calendar (breaks, in-service days, rotating day cycles, weekend classes), places unit and lesson cards, locks some to dates, and the rest reflow automatically when a day is lost. Copying a semester forward to next year re-snaps to the new calendar.
why_hard_to_copy: The reflow engine (locked items, skipped days, rotating day cycles, split periods, year-to-year re-snap) is correctness-critical calendar logic; plenty of planner CRUD apps exist but few handle locking plus bumping correctly.
web_delivery: Next.js PWA on Vercel Hobby; reflow engine runs client-side and works offline via service worker; Supabase free for accounts and plans; PDF/ICS export via browser APIs.
satellite_what: Free tool: paste your school year dates, breaks and cycle (A/B, 6-day) and get a printable day-by-day calendar with the 100th day and instructional-day count.
marketing_where: Teacher Facebook groups; Teachers Pay Teachers community; Homeschool forums (e.g. The Well-Trained Mind); Product Hunt; Instructional coach newsletters
marketing_target: K-12 teachers and homeschool parents who plan lessons by calendar day
marketing_funnel: Free day counter calendar -> add units and lessons -> sign up to save and reflow
cold_outreach: Reply helpfully to public teacher requests for lock/bump features with the free tool.
post_ideas: Why your lesson planner breaks every time a snow day hits (and a way to fix it) | Free instructional-day counter for any school calendar | Copy last year's pacing guide onto this year's calendar in one click
competitors: Common Curriculum; Planbook; Homeschool Planet
notes: The strongest dated evidence is a single thread with 2025 comments; most of the board is old (2015-2020), so the recency rests on that thread plus the Sept 2025 AI-export request. Competitor Planbook already bumps lessons, so differentiation is lock-plus-bump, rotation cycles and a free tier.

name: MediaMover
idea: A browser tool that imports exports from Trakt, Letterboxd, TV Time, StoryGraph, Goodreads and others into one clean library and exports back out to any of them.
description: Users drop their export files into the page; parsers normalise titles, dates, ratings and rewatch counts, match them against open metadata, and let the user review low-confidence matches. The result is a shareable read-only library page plus export files in the format of any target service. Aimed at people leaving or hedging against a tracker that changes pricing or shuts down. The moat is the pile of obscure export formats and matching edge cases.
why_hard_to_copy: Many undocumented export formats, season/episode and edition mapping edge cases, and fuzzy matching with a review step; accumulating tested parsers takes real time.
web_delivery: Static web app with all parsing and matching UI in the browser; Supabase stores only the user's optional shareable library JSON; Vercel serves the pages and a small metadata proxy route.
satellite_what: Free one-file converter, e.g. TV Time CSV to Letterboxd/Trakt-ready CSV, no account.
marketing_where: AlternativeTo; Product Hunt; Hacker News Show HN; Mastodon hashtags for film and book tracking; Trakt and Letterboxd community forums
marketing_target: Heavy movie, TV and book loggers switching or consolidating services
marketing_funnel: Search for 'import X to Y' -> converter -> shareable library page
cold_outreach: Comment on migration threads with a ready converter link.
post_ideas: Move your TV Time history anywhere in a minute | One library for films, shows and books with exports back out | I found 40 duplicate rewatches while merging my tracker exports
competitors: Sofa; Moviebase; Curate; Ryot
notes: Crowded space (Sofa, Curate, Simkl, Trakt, Ryot). Demand evidence all comes from one repo's request stream. Metadata sources such as TMDB have licensing limits for commercial use that must be checked before launch. A competitor page claims TV Time is shutting down in July 2026; I did not verify that.

name: RecipeFixer
idea: Adapt a recipe to what you have: smart scaling, tiny-amount conversions and context-aware substitutions.
description: Paste or enter a recipe and a target (half batch, different pan, missing ingredient); the tool scales eggs by weight, adjusts leavening and spice non-linearly, rounds tiny amounts to real packet or spoon sizes, flags prep ambiguity such as measure-before-grinding, and suggests substitutions that depend on the dish type. The moat is the baking-science rules and substitution matrix, not a linear multiplier.
why_hard_to_copy: Curated non-linear scaling rules and a dish-aware substitution matrix; plain multipliers are trivial, this is not.
web_delivery: Next.js PWA on Vercel; rules in Supabase; all calculations client-side.
satellite_what: Convert ounces or grams of yeast to packets or teaspoons and halve eggs correctly.
marketing_where: Baking forums (The Fresh Loaf, etc.); Facebook baking groups; Cooking blogs; Pinterest; Show HN
marketing_target: Home bakers and cooks adapting recipes
marketing_funnel: Search 'how to halve a cake recipe' -> tool.
cold_outreach: Offer recipe bloggers a free scaling widget.
post_ideas: How to halve a cake recipe without ruining it | 0.09 oz of yeast is how many packets? | Fresh to dried herbs: when the ratio breaks
competitors: Instacart recipe converter; RecipeSage pan converter; Omni Calculator fresh-to-dry herb conversion
notes: Many scalers exist; the differentiator is non-linear rules, which a motivated vibe coder could partly copy. Substitution data needs expert curation. Signals are low-engagement (141-2,223 views).

name: NightTransfer
idea: A guide to getting to and from airports and between airports when trains and buses have stopped.
description: For major airports and city pairs, the page lists last and first services, night buses, taxi or fixed-price options, accessible routes with luggage, and whether you can stay in the airport overnight. The moat is a curated and dated dataset of off-hours alternatives, which general map apps handle poorly and that changes seasonally.
why_hard_to_copy: Hand-checked off-hours service data for airports and inter-airport transfers; maps and trip planners return nothing useful after midnight.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; Supabase tables of airport, mode, last/first service, source URL and verified_at.
marketing_where: FlyerTalk forums; TripAdvisor destination forums; Travel Stack Exchange (answer questions, link only where site rules allow); Facebook expat and digital-nomad groups; Show HN; Product Hunt
marketing_target: Travellers on late-arrival or early-departure itineraries
marketing_funnel: Search 'airport to city after midnight <airport>' -> airport page.
cold_outreach: Pitch city transit blogs and airport-hotel blogs.
post_ideas: Last trains from Heathrow, Gatwick and Stansted by line | Between airports after 8 PM: Osaka, Shanghai, London | Can you sleep in the terminal? Rules by airport
competitors: Airport Transfer Portal late-night airport guides; Tokyo Cheapo Haneda late-night transfer guide
notes: Five different askers; views 390-1,379. Commercial competition for the taxi-intent keywords. Overlaps with AirportRules and could be one product.

name: Manuscript Style Linter
idea: Web linter that checks a LaTeX manuscript and bibliography against a chosen journal's style rules and converts US/UK spelling safely.
description: Upload or paste a .tex and .bib, pick a journal rule pack, and get a report with line references for required macros, citation form, title/section/caption capitalization, code markup and missing bib fields such as DOI, plus a spelling normalizer that leaves math, code, quotes and citations untouched. Aimed at researchers whose papers bounce at editorial check. Hard to copy because the value is hand-curated, expert-maintained rule packs and a LaTeX-aware tokenizer, not generic grammar checking.
why_hard_to_copy: Curated per-journal rule packs plus a LaTeX-aware tokenizer that can skip math, verbatim and citations; generic AI or grammar tools do not know journal macros.
web_delivery: Client-side TypeScript parser on Vercel hobby; rule packs as JSON in the repo; files never leave the browser; Supabase free only for optional rule-pack contributions.
satellite_name: US to UK spelling for LaTeX
satellite_what: Free page that converts American to British spelling in pasted LaTeX while skipping math, code and citations.
marketing_where: TeX Stack Exchange answers; Academia Stack Exchange answers; Overleaf community forum; Society mailing lists for journals with custom LaTeX classes
marketing_target: Researchers and grad students submitting LaTeX papers to specific journals
marketing_funnel: Spelling converter or forum answer -> journal check -> contribute a rule pack for their journal
cold_outreach: Offer journal editorial offices a free rule pack for their house style to cut desk rejections.
post_ideas: Convert American to British spelling in LaTeX without breaking your math | A lint report for the JSS style guide | Why chktex will not catch your journal's rules
competitors: chktex; Paperpal and Writefull
notes: Each journal pack is manual work, so coverage grows slowly and monetization is unclear. Two related but different requests. A related softwarerecs thread (95130, 2026-01-18) wants Overleaf track-changes rendered into the exported PDF, another manuscript workflow gap (needs LaTeX compilation, so not included).

name: BracketForge
idea: Free, no-paywall tournament engine with Swiss, double-elimination and group-to-playoff formats and live spectator pages.
description: Organisers of community game nights, school clubs and local esports events create a bracket without hitting a paywall, using correct Swiss pairing with tiebreaks, double elimination with grand-final reset, seeding byes and multi-stage formats. Players join by link with no account and results update live on a spectator screen. Hard to copy because pairing and tiebreak rules are correctness-critical and the live-sync layer must be reliable at venue Wi-Fi quality.
why_hard_to_copy: Swiss pairing with Buchholz-style tiebreaks, bye handling, double-elimination reset logic and re-seeding after dropouts are rules-engine problems with many edge cases, and live results need dependable realtime sync.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; pairing engine in TypeScript; results and live standings through Supabase Realtime; public read-only spectator URL.
satellite_what: Free page: enter players and results, get next-round Swiss pairings and standings with tiebreaks.
marketing_where: board-game and trading-card-game store Discords; local esports and school club organiser groups; BoardGameGeek forums; itch.io and game-jam communities
marketing_target: Volunteer organisers of weekly game nights and small local tournaments
marketing_funnel: Free pairings page to free tournament creation to paid for branded venue displays
cold_outreach: Message local game-store owners with a free tournament page for their next event.
post_ideas: Swiss pairing explained with a worked example and the rematch bug most apps have | Run a 32-player double-elimination from your phone with no account | Why free bracket apps hit a paywall after you type in all the names
competitors: Challonge; VERXUS; Score7; DART-TV
notes: Paywall pattern is clear but free competitors (VERXUS, Challonge free tier) exist, so differentiation is correctness plus a no-account spectator mode. Guilded signal is context only (shutdown, not a tournament complaint); the AlternativeTo news page does not itself name tournaments. No payments or prize pools to stay outside banned niches.

name: PassportValidity
idea: Look up passport and ID-card validity rules for a destination and trip dates, including the ones airlines enforce.
description: User enters passport expiry date, trip dates, destination and transit points; the tool computes whether the three-month, six-month or other rule is met measured from entry or departure, notes blank-page needs and whether national ID cards are accepted, and cites the official source. The moat is the curated rules table with the 'measured from entry vs departure' detail and ID-card acceptance, which blog lists get wrong or leave stale.
why_hard_to_copy: Hand-curated, cited per-country dataset with careful date logic (months beyond entry vs beyond departure, transit legs, ID cards) and visible last-verified date.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel with Supabase table of country rules and sources; date arithmetic client-side.
satellite_what: Enter expiry date and trip dates to see pass or fail for the most common 3- and 6-month rules.
marketing_where: FlyerTalk forums; TripAdvisor destination forums; Travel Stack Exchange (answer questions, link only where site rules allow); Facebook expat and digital-nomad groups; Show HN; Product Hunt
marketing_target: Travellers with passports close to expiry; families with minors' ID cards
marketing_funnel: Search 'passport 5 months validity <country>' -> page.
cold_outreach: Pitch passport-renewal and travel-document bloggers.
post_ideas: Does your passport need 6 months for Peru? How it is counted | Schengen's 3-month rule: from entry or from departure? | ID cards in the Balkans: which countries accept them near expiry
competitors: Your Mileage May Vary list of countries by remaining validity; The Points Guy six-month rule guide
notes: Crowded field (airline-embedded checkers, blogs). Five askers across the window, moderate views (365-1,419 for most). Value would depend on being more accurate and more current than blogs; weak moat versus Sherpa. Liability disclaimer needed.

name: Course Rescue
idea: Import a Canvas/Common Cartridge or QTI export and turn it into a free, hosted mini-course with auto-graded quizzes.
description: Independent teachers, tutors and homeschool co-ops lost free tools in 2026: Canvas Free-for-Teacher shut down after a final export window in July, Padlet retired its teaching tools, and GitHub Classroom closed. This app imports a .imscc or QTI export in the browser, rebuilds modules, pages and quizzes, and hosts them with a student login-free code link, auto-grading and CSV grade export. Hard to copy because Common Cartridge and QTI exports vary by tool version and quiz question types (numeric tolerance, matching, multi-answer) must be graded correctly.
why_hard_to_copy: Parsing .imscc and QTI variants and reproducing Canvas quiz-question scoring semantics is format-specific, correctness-critical work.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; the export is parsed client-side with a zip library; course JSON in Supabase; grading in Supabase Edge Functions; media kept as links to limit storage.
satellite_what: Free page that converts a QTI/Canvas quiz export into a printable quiz or a CSV question bank.
marketing_where: instructional-design and educator communities; homeschool co-op forums; tutoring and test-prep groups on Facebook; university teaching-and-learning center newsletters
marketing_target: Independent teachers, tutors and instructional designers who relied on Canvas Free-for-Teacher
marketing_funnel: Free converter, then free hosted course for a small class, then paid for larger rosters and branded domains
cold_outreach: Email people who published guides on Canvas Free-for-Teacher with a free import of their sample courses.
post_ideas: I exported my Canvas Free-for-Teacher course, now what? | Turn a Canvas quiz export into a shareable auto-graded quiz | Which free LMS keeps your quiz banks portable
competitors: Google Classroom; Classroom 50; Codio
notes: Shutdown evidence is real but all institutional; I did not find a user thread. One secondary source says Instructure promised a replacement, and one headline suggested access might have been restored after a breach, so the market may be smaller than it looks. Student data handling (accounts, FERPA/COPPA) is a real compliance burden; keep students anonymous with code links.

name: PaverLayout
idea: Generate random-pattern paving or tiling layouts from the real slab sizes with consistent joints and minimal cuts.
description: User enters area and the available slab or tile sizes; the solver tries layouts that keep a constant joint width, avoid awkward slivers, and minimise cut pieces, then shows a printable plan and material counts. The moat is the constraint-solving layout algorithm for mixed modular sizes, which standard grid, running-bond or honeycomb tools do not cover.
why_hard_to_copy: Constraint/bin-packing layout solver for random-pattern modular paving, which needs real algorithm work rather than a CRUD form.
web_delivery: Client-side canvas app (Next.js on Vercel); saved layouts in Supabase; solver in a web worker.
satellite_what: Quick slab count and wastage estimate for a patio area.
marketing_where: DIY and landscaping forums; Garden design Facebook groups; YouTube DIY patio channels; Paving supplier blogs; Show HN
marketing_target: DIY patio builders and small landscapers using multi-size slab packs
marketing_funnel: Search 'random pattern paving layout calculator' -> tool.
cold_outreach: Offer paving suppliers a free pattern generator widget for their kits.
post_ideas: Why your random-pattern patio gets uneven joints, and how to fix the layout | Plan a patio from a 4-size slab pack | Cut less stone: layout tips
competitors: Herron tile planner; Layometry; Calcufloor
notes: Only two SE signals (146 and 1,054 views) and existing planners cover common patterns. Idea is credible technically but demand evidence is thin.

name: PackStation
idea: Tablet-friendly packing screen that turns any order export into pick lists, per-customer pack checklists and box labels for farms, CSAs and food hubs.
description: Hub operators and small farms import an order CSV from whatever shop tool they use, then get an interactive packing screen: filter by storage type (frozen, chilled, dry), customer, producer and pick-up versus delivery, tick items off as packed, and print labels. No payments are handled. Hard part is the per-platform CSV importers and an offline-first sync so it keeps working in a warehouse with bad wifi.
why_hard_to_copy: Needs offline-first sync plus a library of messy export formats from several farm and food-hub platforms; generic CRUD clones will not cover those.
web_delivery: PWA with IndexedDB offline storage and Supabase sync; CSV parsing and label printing done client-side on Vercel hobby.

marketing_target: Small food hub and CSA operators who pack weekly boxes
marketing_funnel: Free label maker -> import orders -> packing screen

post_ideas: How we cut Saturday packing time with a tablet checklist | Free printable CSA box labels | Pack by storage zone: a simple method for small hubs
competitors: Barn2Door; Open Food Network
notes: Only two dated forum signals, both from one community (Open Food Network), and one of them is a vendor-side scoping post, not an end-user complaint. Niche is small; validate with hub operators before building.

name: Spool Stash
idea: A hosted, multi-user filament inventory for 3D printing with barcode and NFC spool scanning and a shared community filament database.
description: Track every spool and remaining weight, scan manufacturer barcodes or open NFC spool tags from a phone to add spools in seconds, and share a library with a print club or print farm. Export spool data to slicer or colour tools. Aimed at hobbyists and small print shops who do not want to run a home server. The curated filament database and tag-format parsing are the moat.
why_hard_to_copy: A hand-maintained filament database (brands, materials, temperatures, colours) and parsing of emerging spool tag standards.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel; Supabase auth, Postgres and row-level security for multi-user spaces; camera barcode scanning via the browser BarcodeDetector API; NFC via Web NFC on Android Chrome only.
satellite_what: Pick a colour and see the closest filaments across brands from the database.
marketing_where: 3D printing forums and Discords; Printables and MakerWorld community comments; Hacker News Show HN; YouTube 3D printing channels; AlternativeTo
marketing_target: Home 3D printer owners and small print farms
marketing_funnel: Colour matcher -> free stash -> invite club members
cold_outreach: Offer print-farm owners a free shared workspace for feedback.
post_ideas: Scan a spool barcode and add it in one second | Stop buying duplicate colours you already own | Share a filament library with your makerspace
competitors: Filamio; Spoolman; Spoolstock

name: ENEX Exit
idea: Convert an Evernote export (.enex) to clean Markdown, Obsidian, Joplin or Apple Notes folders entirely in the browser.
description: Drop one or many multi-GB ENEX files. It streams them, keeps notebooks, tags, dates, attachments, tables, checklists and evernote:// links, and outputs a zip or a folder in the layout of the target app. Aimed at people leaving Evernote after repeated price rises under Bending Spoons. Moat is fidelity of ENML-to-Markdown conversion and large-file streaming, not the UI.
why_hard_to_copy: Converting ENML (HTML-like with embedded resources referenced by hash, nested tables, checkboxes, in-note links) to Markdown faithfully across target apps is full of edge cases, and doing it on multi-GB files in memory-limited browsers needs streaming design.
web_delivery: Static web app on Vercel; ENEX parsed with streaming XML in a Web Worker; output via File System Access API or a streamed zip; no uploads, no server.
satellite_what: Free page that opens an .enex file locally and shows note count, attachment sizes, tables and unsupported content before you convert.
marketing_where: Joplin forum; Obsidian forum and Discord; Hacker News threads on Bending Spoons acquisitions; Lemmy c/selfhosted; AlternativeTo (Evernote alternatives page)
marketing_target: Long-time Evernote users with big archives who are leaving over price.
marketing_funnel: Free converter for up to N notes -> one-time unlock for full archives.

competitors: evernote2md; enex2md; ever2simple; convert.guru ENEX converter; BitRecover Evernote to Markdown
notes: Free CLIs already do the conversion, so the real gap is a no-install, no-upload, GUI path for non-technical people; the demand signal is price anger, not an explicit request for a web converter. Evernote may also change export formats.

name: TankLog Free
idea: Aquarium journal with unlimited free water-test logging, charts, dosing maths and a species list you can extend.
description: AquaticLog introduced a cap of about five to ten logged measurements a month on the free tier, and fish-keeping apps are criticised for small species catalogs, no way to add your own fish, and no incompatibility warnings. The web app logs unlimited parameters per tank, plots trends, calculates dose volumes and water-change maths, and lets users add custom species and check stocking compatibility. Moat: a curated species/compatibility table and correct chemistry calculators (tank volume net of substrate, product dosing, KH/GH/CO2 relationships).
capital_note: Domain; Supabase free and Vercel hobby are enough for logs.
why_hard_to_copy: The logger is simple, but the hand-curated compatibility/dosing data and correct calculators are not; building trust takes community seeding.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel with Supabase auth and tables for tanks, tests and species; charts rendered client-side; installable on a phone for bench-side logging.
satellite_name: Tank dosing and water change calculator
satellite_what: Free calculator for net tank volume, fertiliser/medication dose and water-change percentages.
marketing_where: FishLore and Planted Tank style forums; reef2reef; aquarium YouTube comment sections and Discord servers; Facebook species-focused groups
marketing_target: Freshwater, planted and reef hobbyists who test water weekly.
marketing_funnel: Calculator -> free log -> shareable tank page.
cold_outreach: Offer species-focused forum moderators a free embeddable compatibility checker.
post_ideas: Free tank log with no monthly measurement cap | Stocking checker that lets you add your own species | How to read your nitrate trend chart
competitors: AquaLog; Aquarium Tracker: Tank Manager; AquaMeter
notes: A bare logger is a weekend project, so the plan only works if the curated species/dosing data is the product. At least four independent reviews in one cluster.

name: TableMatch
idea: A local-group board for tabletop and board game hosts to post sessions, GMs to pitch games, and players to RSVP or vote with availability.
description: Local game groups run on WhatsApp or Discord where session requests scroll off screen and GMs cannot pitch one-shots or campaigns with a vote on interest. TableMatch gives each local group one page: GMs post a pitch with dates, players mark availability, a poll shows which pitches have enough interest, and an optional BoardGameGeek collection import shows who owns a wanted game. Moat is the availability-overlap and quorum logic plus the BGG collection/wishlist matching, and the network effect inside each small local group.
capital_note: Domain name only; Supabase free + Vercel hobby cover hosting
why_hard_to_copy: Availability-overlap and minimum-players logic, BGG collection syncing with rate-limit handling, and per-group communities that stick once a local group migrates.
web_delivery: Responsive web app/PWA; Supabase auth + Postgres with row-level security per group; BGG public XML API called from a Vercel serverless function with caching.
satellite_what: Paste several BGG usernames and see which owned games fit the player count and time, plus a shareable availability grid.
marketing_where: BoardGameGeek forums and guilds; Lemmy c/boardgames and c/rpg; Local game store Discords and Facebook groups; Warhorn and Meetup organiser circles
marketing_target: Organisers of local board game and RPG groups with 10-80 members
marketing_funnel: Satellite overlap tool -> group page -> invite link in the existing chat
cold_outreach: Message organisers who publicly complain that WhatsApp or Discord buries session posts
post_ideas: How our 40-person board game hub stopped losing session requests in WhatsApp | Free tool: paste BGG usernames, see what you can play tonight | Template: a GM pitch that gets players to commit
competitors: Kallax; Game Night Picks; Warhorn; MeepleUp
notes: Competitors exist (Kallax, Game Night Picks, MeepleUp), so differentiation must be the GM-pitch plus interest-poll flow for local groups. Check current BGG API terms before building.

name: Stipend Compass
idea: Crowd-verified atlas of PhD and postdoc stipends by country, university and field, with a living-cost ratio so you can tell if an offer is livable.
description: Prospective and current graduate students look up stipends (reported net amounts, teaching supplements, tuition waivers) and see each one divided by a local living-wage figure, with a 'can I live on this offer' check. Submissions are verified by email domain or offer-letter attestation and shown as ranges. Hard to copy because the asset is a curated, community-verified dataset with a consistent methodology, which cannot be generated in a weekend.
why_hard_to_copy: Verified crowdsourced dataset and consistent methodology (net vs gross, per field, per university); network effects once students contribute.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel hobby with a Supabase free Postgres table of submissions, row-level security and a moderation queue; living-wage reference data as a static table.
satellite_what: Single page: enter stipend, city and household size, get the ratio to a living wage and a plain verdict.

marketing_target: Prospective PhD applicants, international students and postdocs comparing offers

notes: One request with good views (1.35k). Data quality and moderation are the real work; avoid computing taxes (use reported net figures) to stay clear of the tax ban. A free, reusable living-wage reference source per country is not verified.

name: SheetSalvage
idea: Drag-and-drop tool that salvages data from corrupted .xlsx/.xlsm files entirely in the browser, with nothing uploaded.
description: Reads a damaged OOXML package with a tolerant parser (broken or missing zip directory, malformed sheet XML, lost shared strings), lists which sheets and cells are recoverable and exports a clean workbook or CSVs. Spreadsheets with business data never leave the machine, unlike online repair services. Hard to copy because tolerant zip/XML salvage and handling real-world corruption modes (crash during save, sync conflicts, script damage) needs a corpus of broken files and a lot of edge-case work.
why_hard_to_copy: Lenient OOXML and zip recovery with a growing corpus of real corruption cases; most clones just call a strict spreadsheet library that fails on damaged files.
web_delivery: Static site on Vercel hobby; fflate/JSZip-style tolerant unzip plus a custom lenient XML reader in a web worker; no server, no storage.
satellite_what: Drop a file and see exactly what is wrong (missing content types, bad relationships, truncated sheet) without repairing.
marketing_where: MrExcel forum threads on corrupt files; Super User and Microsoft Q&A answers; SEO long tail for 'xlsx corrupted' error messages
marketing_target: Office workers and small-business owners with a damaged workbook
marketing_funnel: Search for the error -> free diagnosis -> salvage export -> optional paid batch or donation
cold_outreach: Answer help threads with a no-upload recovery option and a short demo gif.
post_ideas: Excel says the file is corrupt: what the error actually means | Recover an xlsx without uploading it anywhere | How shared-drive conflicts corrupt spreadsheets
competitors: OfficeRecovery online; Wondershare Repairit; WPS File Repair
notes: One signal (decent views). No browser-only repair tool turned up in my search, which supports the gap, but recovery success rate is the whole product and cannot be verified without a test corpus. Competitors are mostly paid desktop vendors.

name: PracticeLoop
idea: Free web practice planner for musicians that cycles an exercise through all 12 keys and ladders tempo, with an accurate browser metronome and a shareable routine for teachers.
description: Modacity users report that after a redesign the free tier limits practice items and lists and hides the history, and that you cannot create one item across many keys; users of Practice Space want to enter time without running a timer and see longer-term graphs. PracticeLoop lets you define an exercise once and run it through all keys or a circle-of-fourths order, raise tempo in steps automatically, log time manually or by timer, and share a routine link with a teacher. Moat is modest: Web Audio scheduling accuracy and key-cycling logic.
why_hard_to_copy: Sample-accurate Web Audio metronome scheduling and key-cycle/tempo-ladder logic are fiddly; the logging itself is easy to copy, so the moat is the practice engine and teacher sharing.

satellite_what: Enter a pattern and get a transposed printable page through all keys.
marketing_where: jazz and guitar teacher forums; TalkBass and Saxontheweb style forums; music teacher Facebook groups; YouTube music-teacher channel communities
marketing_target: Self-taught and student instrumentalists plus their private teachers.

competitors: Modacity; PitchPlay; Andante / Practice Log
notes: Low copy-resistance (trackers are easy). Only the engine and teacher sharing differentiate.

name: Local Cull
idea: Cull and rate thousands of RAW photos straight from a card in the browser, writing Lightroom-compatible XMP sidecars, with no upload.
description: Open a folder of RAW files with the File System Access API; the app reads each camera's embedded JPEG preview, lets you flag, rate and reject with keyboard shortcuts at full speed, compares burst frames side by side, and writes XMP sidecars so Lightroom, Capture One or darktable see the choices. Aimed at photographers on Windows or Chromebooks who cannot use Mac-only culling tools. Moat is multi-format RAW preview extraction and sidecar compatibility.
why_hard_to_copy: Needs parsers for embedded previews across CR2/CR3/NEF/ARW/RAF/ORF/RW2/DNG containers and XMP rules that Lightroom honors; speed with 3,000+ files in browser memory is non-trivial.
web_delivery: Static web app on Vercel; Chromium File System Access API for read/write; Web Workers decode previews; no server and no upload; optional Supabase for settings.
satellite_what: Drag a RAW file and see its embedded preview and EXIF locally, plus a check of which camera formats are supported.

marketing_target: Event and wedding photographers and enthusiasts shooting RAW on Windows or Chromebook.

cold_outreach: Offer to cull a shoot for forum members as a demo and ask for feedback.

competitors: Imagin Raw; QuickRawPicker; PixRater; photopipe.app
notes: Demand is inferred from a Windows-version request plus a paid cloud competitor existing; not an explicit request for a browser tool. Chromium-only API. Camera RAW container formats change with new models.

name: Signature Shop
idea: Turn any PDF into print-ready signatures or booklets for hobby bookbinding and zines, with creep, duplex flip and fold guides.
description: Upload a PDF locally, pick paper size, signature size (folio, quarto, octavo or saddle-stitch), paper thickness and your printer's duplex behavior; it imposes the pages, applies creep, adds fold marks, sewing-hole marks and a test page, and gives a vector PDF to print on a home printer. Aimed at hobby bookbinders, zine makers and people printing public-domain books. Moat is the imposition and creep math plus per-printer duplex quirks.
why_hard_to_copy: Correct imposition for multi-section sewn bindings, creep compensation by paper caliper, duplex flip modes and cut/fold marks is niche domain logic that a generic prompt gets wrong; but one free browser imposition tool already exists, so this is a hobby-focused refinement.
web_delivery: Static web app on Vercel using pdf-lib in the browser; no uploads; settings saved in localStorage or Supabase for account holders.
satellite_what: Enter page count and get the printing order and blank pages needed for booklets or signatures.
marketing_where: Bookbinding YouTube channel comment sections; Zine-making communities and Discords; Lemmy c/bookbinding style communities; Hacker News Show HN; Etsy seller forums for handmade journals
marketing_target: Hobby bookbinders, zine makers, people printing public-domain books at home.
marketing_funnel: Free calculator -> free imposer for small page counts -> saved printer profiles.
cold_outreach: Offer printer-profile test sheets to bookbinding channel creators.
post_ideas: Print and bind a 300-page book at home: imposition explained | Creep calculator for sewn signatures | Duplex flip settings that ruin a signature, and how to test yours
competitors: WaveSpeed PDF Imposition; pdfimpose; callas pdfToolbox Imposition
notes: Small audience; demand shown by two comments in one thread. Existing free tools cover the basic booklet case.

name: Duo Pose Studio
idea: A browser posing mannequin for multiple figures that interact (hug, fight, hold hands), shareable by link.
description: Artists want pose-reference sites that work for more than one person in frame and are not just a Pinterest board. A 3D mannequin tool with a library of hand-authored two-figure interaction poses, contact constraints and camera angles, running client side, fills that. The ability to save a scene as a link avoids storing images.
why_hard_to_copy: Needs a hand-authored library of believable two-figure poses with contact constraints (inverse kinematics), which takes art and rigging skill.
web_delivery: Three.js app on Vercel; poses as small JSON; scenes saved in the URL or a Supabase row.
satellite_what: Daily random mannequin pose with a timer for gesture practice.
marketing_where: Art practice Discords and Bluesky/X art tags; Comic and illustration communities; Product Hunt
marketing_target: Illustrators and comic artists who need two-person reference.
marketing_funnel: Daily pose page, then the studio.
cold_outreach: Ask art-tutorial creators to try the duo poses for a video.
post_ideas: Free hug and hand-holding pose references from every angle | Duo gesture drawing timer
competitors: Posemy.art; Magic Poser
notes: Two posts. Posemy.art already has a large library and may cover multi-figure scenes; the real gap is unverified.

name: Deck Room
idea: A web spaced-repetition system that opens Anki decks, runs on locked-down school networks and gives teachers class accounts.
description: Import .apkg decks (note types, cloze, images, audio) into a browser app with FSRS scheduling, offline review and sync. Teachers create a class, push decks to students who join by code, and see who is reviewing. It exists because Anki's ownership moved to AnkiHub and teachers say a full-featured web client would solve deployment on restricted networks. Moat is faithful Anki import and card rendering plus classroom features.
why_hard_to_copy: Faithful import of Anki's package formats (SQLite, newer protobuf/zstd variants), note-type templates, cloze and media is a long tail of edge cases; adding multi-user class management and FSRS on top is more work than a weekend vibe-coded flashcard app.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel; .apkg parsed client-side (zip + SQLite via sql.js, media kept in IndexedDB); progress and class membership sync through Supabase free tier.
satellite_what: Free page that opens an .apkg locally and shows cards, note types and media without installing Anki.
marketing_where: Anki forums (forums.ankiweb.net); Language-teacher and med-school communities; Hacker News Show HN; Lemmy language-learning communities; Teacher Discord and Mastodon
marketing_target: Teachers and self-learners who rely on Anki decks but cannot install apps (school Chromebooks, managed devices).
marketing_funnel: Free deck viewer -> free personal web SRS -> class accounts for teachers.
cold_outreach: Reach teachers who publish SRS-in-class write-ups with a pilot class.
post_ideas: Study your Anki decks on a school Chromebook with no install | Class accounts for spaced repetition, no emails collected | What AnkiHub taking over Anki means for classroom use
competitors: Anki / AnkiWeb; awesome-fsrs list of FSRS apps; Native FSRS apps such as Avorio and Discito (Anki alternatives list); Best Anki alternatives roundup
notes: Signals come from one thread but three independent commenters. Supabase free storage (1 GB) limits hosted media, so keep media client-side or cap deck sizes. Anki's package format can change. Teacher's own libreSRS project is a possible competitor.

name: Table Fill
idea: Small-group host kit for recurring game nights and meetups: RSVP no-show forecasting, a waitlist that promotes people automatically, and an activity picker that fits whoever shows up.
description: Hosts of recurring meetups say they cannot predict attendance and many games break at the wrong player count, and the leading platform has become expensive for organisers. Table Fill shows an expected-turnout range from each group's RSVP history, auto-promotes waitlisted people and suggests games from a shared library that work for the confirmed head-count, with a fallback pick if the count drops. Aimed at hosts of board-game, run and hobby groups; the moat is the attendance model and player-count game data, not the event page.
why_hard_to_copy: Per-group attendance forecasting from RSVP history and a player-count-aware game/activity matcher need curated game data and modelling; not just an events CRUD. A network of small hosts adds a data moat over time.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel, Supabase for groups, RSVPs and history; responsive PWA with email reminders from a free-tier email API.
satellite_what: Enter player count and time available; get board games that suit, with a backup if one person drops out.
marketing_where: Board-game cafe and club organiser groups; Local run-club and hobby group chats; BoardGameGeek forums; Hacker News
marketing_target: Volunteer hosts of weekly or monthly hobby meetups.
marketing_funnel: Free picker -> create a recurring group -> forecast and waitlist features.
cold_outreach: Message group hosts who post 'we have two spots open' with a free waitlist link.
post_ideas: How many people will actually show up? A host's cheat sheet | Games that work at 3, 4 and 5 players | Running a meetup without paying per member
competitors: Radius; Meetup; Luma
notes: Meetup-alternative space is contested (Radius, Luma); the player-count and forecast angle is the only differentiator. Game data from BoardGameGeek may need an API token or a hand-curated starter list (check their current terms before depending on it).

name: TripPaste
idea: Paste or drop travel confirmations and get a clean itinerary with a calendar feed, without needing an email-sync service.
description: Travellers paste confirmation emails, upload .eml files or PDFs, and the app extracts flights, hotels, trains and car rentals using hand-built per-supplier parsers, then builds a day-by-day itinerary, time-zone-correct ICS feed and shareable page. It targets people frustrated that email auto-import in the big itinerary apps stopped working or duplicates calendar entries. Hard to copy because accurate extraction from many airline, hotel and rail confirmation formats is a maintained library of parsers and edge cases such as time zones and multi-leg trips.
why_hard_to_copy: A growing, tested library of supplier-specific confirmation parsers with correct time-zone and multi-leg handling, which generic LLM-free code cannot guess.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; parsing runs in the browser (pdf.js for PDFs, text rules for emails); itineraries stored in Supabase with a public share link and ICS route.
satellite_what: Free page: paste one confirmation and download an .ics file with correct time zones.
marketing_where: FlyerTalk and travel-hacking forums; digital nomad and family-travel Facebook groups; Product Hunt; points-and-miles blogs
marketing_target: Frequent leisure and business travellers who dislike paid itinerary subscriptions
marketing_funnel: Free paste-to-ICS page, then free trip pages, then paid for shared group trips and offline PDF packs
cold_outreach: Ask travel bloggers to test it with their messiest multi-leg confirmations.
post_ideas: Why your itinerary app puts a flight at the wrong time zone | Paste a booking email, get a calendar feed: no inbox access needed | Which airline emails parse cleanly and which break everything
competitors: TripIt; Wanderlog; Tripsy; Flighty
notes: Signals are App Store reviews on two apps plus one Trustpilot review, medium count but not yet independent web-based requests. Without inbound email processing the product is paste/upload only, which is less magical than TripIt; the uncorroborated 'TripIt cut third-party sync' claim is flagged. Parser upkeep is a long tail.

name: Kinship Explorer
idea: Upload a GEDCOM file and see exactly how any two people in the tree are related, including in-laws and step relatives, with culture-aware names and kinship terms.
description: Everything runs in the browser: parse the family tree file, pick two people, and get the path, the relationship name in the user's language, and a diagram. Name display can follow local conventions such as patronymics or surname-first order. Anniversary and birthday lists can be exported as a calendar file. Hard to copy because kinship terms and name conventions differ by culture and in-law logic is fiddly.
why_hard_to_copy: Correctness-critical kinship logic (half, step, in-law, multiple spouses) plus per-language relationship terms and name-order formats; client-side parsing of messy GEDCOM variants.
web_delivery: Static web app on Vercel; GEDCOM parsed and queried entirely in the browser (no upload, no storage); Supabase only for optional saved views and share links.
satellite_what: Tiny free page: paste two lineage descriptions or upload a small file and get the plain-language relationship.
marketing_where: WikiTree G2G forum; Genealogy Stack Exchange; Gramps community forum; Facebook genealogy groups; AlternativeTo
marketing_target: Family historians and the relatives who ask them 'how are we related'
marketing_funnel: Relationship question -> explorer -> saved tree view
cold_outreach: Answer relationship questions on genealogy Q&A sites with a link showing the path.
post_ideas: Why your spouse's cousin is not 'not related' in your tree | Explain any two people's relationship in one click | Patronymic and surname-first names without breaking your GEDCOM
competitors: GEDminer Kinship Explorer; Topola Viewer; Family Viewer
notes: All five signals come from one project's tracker, though several are recently active. Existing client-side viewers (GEDminer) overlap; the differentiator would be in-law/step logic, multi-language terms, and name formats.

name: Marches Hub
idea: A West Marches / open-table sandbox campaign site where players post session logs and drop pins on a shared map, with each player only seeing what their characters have discovered.
description: A GM running a sandbox campaign wants players to add their own logs, wiki edits and drawings, plus a map with information pins, without wrestling a self-hosted wiki or forcing everyone onto Google/Discord accounts. Marches Hub gives each campaign a magic-link player roster, discovery-gated map pins (a pin is only visible once a character has been there), an expedition board where any player can call a session, and a rotating-roster rule set typical of West Marches play. The moat is the per-player knowledge-state permission model plus open-table scheduling rules that general wiki tools do not model.
capital_note: Domain name only; Supabase free and Vercel hobby cover hosting at this scale.
why_hard_to_copy: Per-player discovery-gated visibility (row-level security over pins, logs and map layers) and open-table scheduling logic are fiddly to get right; a generic notes or wiki clone does not cover them. Small-niche community word of mouth also matters.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel hobby; Supabase Postgres with row-level security for per-player visibility; Leaflet image-map for hand-drawn maps; magic-link login so players need no Google/Discord account.
satellite_what: Free single-page tool for open-table GMs: players propose a session, others sign up, and it tracks who is available and which characters are in town.
marketing_where: EN World forums; RPG.net forums; RPGGeek; itch.io TTRPG community; West Marches blogs and Discord servers
marketing_target: GMs running open-table or sandbox campaigns with 6+ rotating players
marketing_funnel: Free expedition board in forum threads, then upgrade to the full hub for the whole campaign
cold_outreach: Reply in threads where GMs describe running a West Marches game and offer a free hub for their campaign.
post_ideas: How I let players discover my hex map one pin at a time | A no-account campaign site for West Marches games | Why your sandbox campaign wiki should not need a Discord login
competitors: Kanka; Legend Keeper; World Anvil; Obsidian Portal
notes: Single recent thread (page 1 only read; later pages not checked). Map image uploads can hit Supabase free storage limits, so cap image size. Campaign-wiki space is crowded; the differentiator is discovery-gated visibility, not wiki features.

name: Moon & Sun Alignment Finder
idea: Free PWA that tells you the next dates and times the Sun or Moon will sit at a chosen spot in the sky (landmark, skyline notch), including terrain horizon.
description: Pick a location and aim at a landmark (compass or tap on a map/skyline) or enter azimuth and elevation, and get the next several dates when the Moon, full Moon or Sun lines up within a tolerance, plus a yearly sun-path view to judge shade from trees and buildings. Aimed at photographers and gardeners who want it free on Android and iOS. Hard to copy only moderately: ephemeris math is available in libraries, the craft is the reverse search with tolerance, refraction and a terrain horizon profile.
why_hard_to_copy: Reverse ephemeris search with tolerance, refraction and terrain-horizon masking is more work than a sun-position viewer; incumbent apps keep it behind paid mobile apps.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel hobby: astronomy-engine in the browser, DeviceOrientation/compass for aiming, free public terrain tiles for the horizon, Supabase free for saved spots.
satellite_what: Tiny page: enter a place name and get dates the Moon rises or sets at the same bearing as a landmark.
marketing_where: Photography Stack Exchange answers; Local photography club newsletters; Astrophotography forums such as Cloudy Nights; Garden planning groups on Facebook
marketing_target: Landscape photographers and gardeners wanting free sun/moon planning
marketing_funnel: Moon-over-landmark page -> finder -> saved spots -> shared plans with friends
cold_outreach: Offer local photographers a pre-computed alignment sheet for a famous skyline.
post_ideas: When will the full Moon sit on top of your local landmark? (free tool) | Plan a yearly sun path to see garden shade | Reverse ephemeris search explained
competitors: The Photographer's Ephemeris (TPE); PhotoPills
notes: Honest doubt: TPE and PhotoPills already do the reverse search in paid/mobile form, so demand is 'free web' rather than 'new capability'. Both SE signals have low engagement. Without terrain-horizon masking the product is trivially copyable.

name: Fairy Problem Bench
idea: Browser solver for fairy chess problems with a visual editor for custom pieces and arbitrary board sizes.
description: Problem composers and solvers set up a position, define their own fairy pieces (leapers, riders, hoppers) with a visual move editor, pick a stipulation such as helpmate in n or series mover, and solve entirely in the browser. Problems are saved and shared by link. Hard to copy because it means porting or wrapping a serious solver (Popeye-class) to WebAssembly and exposing custom piece definitions, plus knowledge of problem-chess conventions.
why_hard_to_copy: Niche domain expertise and a WASM port of a complex C solver (or a custom TypeScript solver) with user-defined pieces; almost no one can clone it quickly.
web_delivery: WebAssembly solver in a web worker, static site on Vercel hobby; Supabase free for saved and shared problems.
marketing_where: Chess Stack Exchange; Julia's Fairies (fairy chess site); Problem chess composer communities and mailing lists
marketing_target: Fairy chess composers and solvers
marketing_funnel: Shared solvable problem links circulate within the small community
cold_outreach: Offer to host a composer's collection as live, solvable diagrams.
post_ideas: Define your own fairy piece and solve in the browser | Helpmate in 4 with a custom hopper: shareable diagram | Popeye in your browser (without installing)
competitors: Jacobi; Fairy-Stockfish WebAssembly; Popeye and other problem software (overview)
notes: Tiny audience and single signal; included because the moat is high and cost near zero. Popeye is open source on GitHub but I did not verify its licence, so a port may force a compatible licence. A chess variant web app (Chessperiment) was announced on the same site on 2026-01-28 (https://chess.stackexchange.com/questions/47619/ive-created-a-chess-variant-webapp-for-highly-custom-chess-variants-feedback), showing adjacent interest but for playing, not solving.

name: Parts Bin Online
idea: A hosted electronics parts inventory with SI-unit-aware parameters, free-storage-slot finder and order import from distributors.
description: Hobbyists log components with parameters that understand units (100nF equals 0.1uF), find the next free drawer or reel slot, and import DigiKey or Mouser orders instead of typing each line. Projects keep a BOM with stock check and cost roll-up, printable as a pick list. Aimed at electronics hobbyists and small hardware teams who will not run a server. SI-aware search and distributor importers are the moat.
capital_note: Domain; distributor API keys are free to register.
why_hard_to_copy: Unit-normalising parameter search, distributor order and BOM parsing, and storage-location logic are domain-specific and fiddly.
web_delivery: Web app on Vercel with Supabase Postgres; distributor lookups via free distributor APIs through serverless routes; order-CSV import parsed client-side; label printing through browser print CSS.
satellite_name: SI Value Converter and Resistor/Capacitor Code Decoder
satellite_what: Free page decoding component markings and converting nF/uF/pF.
marketing_where: EEVblog forum; Hackaday comments and Hackaday.io; KiCad forum; Hacker News Show HN; AlternativeTo
marketing_target: Electronics hobbyists and small hardware teams
marketing_funnel: Decoder page -> inventory -> BOM stock check
cold_outreach: Offer makerspaces a shared free workspace.
post_ideas: Import your DigiKey order into an inventory in one paste | Is a 0.1uF the same as a 100nF? Your parts database should know | Find the next free drawer automatically
competitors: Binner; InvenTree; KiCost; BOMER
notes: Strong self-hosted alternatives (Binner, InvenTree, Part-DB) mean the gap is 'no hosting needed'. Distributor API terms and rate limits need checking.

name: Mesh Pair
idea: Design complete 3D-printable gear trains in the browser, including the mating gear, and export STL, STEP and DXF.
description: You choose module, tooth counts, pressure angle and a printer-tolerance preset; it builds matched gears with correct center distance, backlash and tooth-profile corrections, shows them meshing, and exports STL, STEP and DXF. Covers spur, helical/herringbone, rack and planetary sets. Hard to copy because of the gear math and in-browser STEP export.
why_hard_to_copy: Involute geometry with profile shift, undercut avoidance, contact ratio and FDM backlash tuning is correctness-critical; STEP export from the browser needs a CAD kernel in WASM.
web_delivery: Static app on Vercel; geometry in JS/WASM (three.js preview, OpenCascade WASM for STEP); designs saved as URL parameters, optional saved designs in Supabase.
satellite_name: Gear Ratio and Center Distance Calculator
satellite_what: Single-page calculator: module, teeth, ratio, center distance, with a warning when two gears will not mesh.
marketing_where: Printables and MakerWorld model descriptions; Hackaday.io; Lemmy c/3dprinting; Prusa and Bambu community forums; Hacker News Show HN
marketing_target: Hobby 3D printer owners, robotics students, clock and automata makers.
marketing_funnel: Free calculator -> free STL generator -> saved designs and STEP export unlock.
cold_outreach: Reply to gear-related questions on maker forums with a prebuilt shareable design link.
post_ideas: Generate a matching gear pair that actually fits, with printer tolerance built in | Why your printed gears bind: backlash and profile shift explained | Export STEP gears from a browser tab
competitors: MakerWorld Parametric Gear Generator; geargen; MatterHackers Gear Creator; Hessmer involute spur gear builder / museum copy
notes: Signals are three comments in one thread (single independent source). Free OpenSCAD customizers are strong competitors; the opening is mating-pair design plus STEP/DXF export. OpenCascade WASM bundle is large but fits Vercel hobby static hosting.

name: Canvas Snippet Kit
idea: Accessible, Canvas-safe HTML components (accordions, tabs, callouts, study cards) that teachers paste into the LMS page editor.
description: A web tool with templates that survive the Canvas HTML sanitizer, using native details/summary and plain semantic HTML instead of stripped scripts. Teachers fill a form, preview with Canvas-like styling and copy the code. Moat is tested knowledge of what each LMS keeps or strips plus accessibility checks.
why_hard_to_copy: Value is an up-to-date, tested map of what Canvas, Moodle and others sanitize plus accessible patterns; low technical moat, mostly maintenance knowledge.
web_delivery: Static web app on Vercel; templates as JSON; live preview in an iframe; copy-to-clipboard output; no accounts.
satellite_what: Paste HTML and see which tags, styles and scripts Canvas would strip.
marketing_where: Canvas Community forums; Instructional design Slack/Discord groups; Higher-ed LinkedIn groups; Moodle forums; Hacker News Show HN
marketing_target: Teachers and instructional designers who hand-edit LMS pages.
marketing_funnel: Free snippet library -> custom branded theme pack.
cold_outreach: Reply to Canvas Community 'accordion not working' threads.
post_ideas: Canvas accordions without JavaScript | What Canvas strips from your HTML | Accessible tabs for LMS pages
competitors: Canvas Community accordion/tab code threads; Canvas Ideas: tabs and accordions in the RCE toolbar
notes: Only one HN signal; support comes from Canvas Community threads I did not date-check. LMS vendors could ship native blocks. Likely easy to copy once public.

name: MealMerge
idea: A meal planner whose shopping list correctly adds up the same ingredient across recipes, converts units, and optionally subtracts what is in your pantry.
description: Plan the week from your saved recipes and get one shopping list where 2 eggs plus 3 eggs becomes 5, grams and cups are reconciled by ingredient, and pantry items can be taken off. Also supports adding a whole day or a whole week to the list in one click and notes on list items. Aimed at households and shared student kitchens who find recipe managers' lists naive. The moat is an ingredient parser plus unit and density conversion rules.
why_hard_to_copy: Accurate ingredient parsing and unit/density conversion across metric and imperial with fuzzy ingredient matching; a hand-built conversion table is slow to get right.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel with Supabase Postgres; ingredient parsing and merging run in the browser; household sharing via Supabase auth and row-level security.
satellite_what: Free converter for cups, grams, ounces and sticks of butter by ingredient.
marketing_where: Product Hunt; AlternativeTo; meal-prep and budget-cooking communities; Pinterest recipe boards; Hacker News Show HN
marketing_target: Households, roommates and meal-preppers who plan weekly dinners
marketing_funnel: Unit converter -> import recipes by URL -> weekly plan -> shared list
cold_outreach: Answer 'combine ingredients across recipes' questions with a demo list.
post_ideas: Why your meal planner lists eggs twice | Plan the week in 5 minutes and get one clean shopping list | Roommate dinners without spreadsheet chaos
competitors: Cooklist; MealBoard; Meal Master Plan; Mealie / Tandoor / KitchenOwl
notes: Engagement per thread is modest; the strength is that the same gap appears across Grocy, Mealie, Tandoor and RecipeSage. Several app-store competitors do part of this, but I found no documentation of how they handle unit conversion.

name: RailFareJapan
idea: Plan which Japan rail tickets to buy: pass vs individual reserved tickets vs regional passes, including advance-purchase quirks.
description: User enters legs and dates; the tool compares the national pass with individual reserved fares and regional passes, flags trains excluded from passes, voucher-exchange quirks (for example airport express tickets bought online), and busy periods such as Golden Week. The moat is a curated fare and rules dataset, which is hard because there is no free fare API.
capital_note: Domain only; fare data entry is own time.
why_hard_to_copy: Curated fare tables and special-case rules (excluded trains, reservation windows, voucher exchanges) that need manual upkeep and Japan-specific knowledge.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; fare tables and rules in Supabase; the comparison runs client-side.
marketing_where: Japan travel forums (Japan-Guide forum, TripAdvisor Japan); Facebook Japan travel groups; Travel blogs; Show HN; Product Hunt
marketing_target: First-time Japan visitors planning multi-city trips
marketing_funnel: Search 'JR pass worth it for <itinerary>' -> calculator.
cold_outreach: Pitch Japan bloggers who currently publish static comparison tables.
post_ideas: JR pass or single tickets for Tokyo-Kyoto-Osaka? Worked examples | Golden Week rail booking: what actually sells out | Skyliner voucher: buy online or at the counter?
competitors: JR Pass worth-it guides; ShopBack JR pass vs single tickets
notes: Weakest data story: no free fare feed, so the dataset must be built manually and goes stale, and the JR pass price changed in 2026 per one guide. Four signals, one with decent engagement (10 score, 2,519 views). Included but flagged low.

name: Many Sentences
idea: A spaced-repetition vocabulary trainer that shows a different real example sentence, with audio, every time you review a word.
description: Each word card draws from a pool of real sentences (for example from the Tatoeba corpus under its CC license) matched by lemma and sorted by difficulty, read aloud by the browser's text-to-speech or native recordings where licensed. Reviews are scheduled with FSRS. Aimed at learners who say fixed example sentences get memorized instead of the word. Moat is the curated word-to-sentence index per language.
why_hard_to_copy: The value is a curated, licence-clean word-to-sentence index with lemma matching and difficulty grading per language (Japanese and Chinese need tokenization), which is data work, not UI.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel with offline review (IndexedDB); per-language sentence packs shipped as compressed static files; progress sync via Supabase free tier.
satellite_what: Free lookup: type a word and see graded real sentences with audio for that language.
marketing_where: Language learning Discords; Hacker News Show HN; Lemmy language-learning communities; Anki forums (forums.ankiweb.net); ProductHunt
marketing_target: Self-taught learners of Japanese, Spanish, French and similar using Anki or Duolingo.
marketing_funnel: Free sentence finder -> free trainer for one language -> more languages.
cold_outreach: Answer 'how do I stop memorizing the sentence instead of the word' threads.
post_ideas: Stop memorizing the example sentence: one word, many real sentences | Audio-first vocabulary review, no AI, free | How I graded 200k Tatoeba sentences by difficulty
competitors: tatoeba-to-anki; ankipy-language-examples; AudioStudy audio flashcards; Loudwalk
notes: Core works without AI. Demand comes from two commenters in one thread plus a related Show HN. FSRS has open-source implementations so scheduling is easy; the moat is only the data pipeline. Tatoeba audio coverage is patchy, so TTS quality is a risk.

name: Font Stand-In
idea: Find open-licensed look-alikes for a commercial font (with full CJK coverage) when a font license suddenly becomes unaffordable.
